mainTopic: Ending the fasting discussion and opening פרק מי שהוציאוהו: a person or produce that leaves the תחום against its will
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about fasting on ערב שבת. The גמרא resolves a contradiction with 'before he heard / after he heard' and rules that one fasts and completes the fast. Then the chapter בכל מערבין ends, and the new chapter מי שהוציאוהו begins. Its משנה teaches that a person carried out of his תחום by נכרים or a רוח רעה has only four אמות, but if he is brought back it is as if he never left. The משנה also records a dispute, illustrated by a story of the sages on a ship, about a person placed in a walled city or an animal pen. The גמרא adds several ברייתות of 'three things', each with its practical lesson. It then works through רב נחמן's ruling about leaving or returning on purpose, and through רבה's leniency based on כבוד הבריות. The amud ends with רב פפא's rule that produce returned to the תחום keeps its place, a challenge from תנאים, and the start of a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof that רב יהודה's ruling did not cover every case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its limited reading of רב יהודה's ruling. If he had ruled on all the cases, he would have answered רבה's question about fasting on ערב שבת, but he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think רב יהודה meant his ruling for all the cases, that is a problem: רבה asked רב יהודה about this very question, and he did not answer him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it limited רב יהודה's ruling to only some of the cases. It points out that רב יהודה could not answer רבה's question about fasting on ערב שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is simple: if רב יהודה had a clear ruling that covered ערב שבת, he would have answered when רבה asked. His silence suggests he had no ruling on that case. So his statement must apply only to the other cases.

keyTerms.meaning: If it should enter your mind (if you were to think)
On all of them (all the cases)
He asked him (raised a question to him)
And he did not resolve it for him (gave no answer)

phrases.english: For if it should enter your mind that he meant all of them,
phrases.notes: That is, if you think רב יהודה's ruling covered all the cases, including ערב שבת.

phrases.aramaic: הָא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבָּה מֵרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: didn't רבה ask this of רב יהודה,
and he did not answer him!
phrases.notes: His silence shows he had no clear ruling at that time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the limited reading of רב יהודה's ruling that the גמרא proposed on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רב יהודה's ruling (that the הלכה follows the חכמים) did not include the case of fasting on ערב שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה asked רב יהודה about fasting on ערב שבת, and רב יהודה did not answer.

steps.title: Counter-challenge: the same thing happened with רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof. רבה also asked רב הונא and got no answer, yet מר זוטרא reports a clear ruling from רב הונא. So silence at one time does not show that the teacher never had a ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, what about what מר זוטרא taught in the name of רב הונא: 'The הלכה is that one fasts and completes the fast'? Didn't רבה ask רב הונא about this, and he did not answer him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from the last step. It shows that the same logic would create a contradiction about רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that if a teacher once could not answer a question, he never had a ruling on it. But רב הונא also did not answer רבה, and we still have a clear ruling from רב הונא through מר זוטרא. So the assumption must be wrong, or else the רב הונא case is contradictory too.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turning the logic back on the questioner)
He taught publicly (expounded)
In the name of
He fasts and completes the fast (until nightfall)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase וּלְטַעְמָיךְ does not mean the גמרא now agrees there is a problem with רב יהודה. It shows that the logic of the proof would also create an impossible problem elsewhere, so the proof itself is weak.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, what about what Mar Zutra taught
phrases.notes: The גמרא turns the questioner's own logic against him.

phrases.english: in the name of Rav Huna:
The halacha is that one fasts and completes the fast.
phrases.notes: This refers to fasting on ערב שבת.

phrases.aramaic: הָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבָּה מֵרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Didn't Rabba ask this of Rav Huna,
and he did not answer him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in Step 1 by showing that its logic leads to a contradiction about רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in Step 1 that a teacher's failure to answer רבה proves he never had a ruling on the question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same pattern exists with רב הונא: he did not answer רבה, yet he clearly ruled 'מתענה ומשלים' according to מר זוטרא. So failing to answer once does not prove there was never a ruling.

steps.title: Before he heard the ruling and after he heard it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves both cases the same way. Each teacher could not answer רבה before he heard רב's ruling, and he ruled clearly after he heard it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you must say: this question was asked before he heard the ruling, and this statement was made after he heard it. Here too, with רב יהודה: this question was before he heard the ruling, and this statement was after he heard it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction with a timing explanation. The teacher was unsure at first and later learned the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's questions came before רב הונא and רב יהודה heard רב's ruling, so they had no answer. Their clear statements came later, after they heard it. This removes the contradiction for רב הונא and also cancels the proof from Step 1, so רב יהודה's ruling can include ערב שבת after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introducing the real explanation)
Before he heard it
After he heard it
Here too (applying the same answer)

steps.whatToRemember: A teacher's earlier silence does not contradict his later clear ruling. He may have heard the ruling only afterward. This 'before he heard / after he heard' answer appears in many places in ש״ס.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer removes the proof that רב יהודה's ruling was limited. It opens the way for the clear הלכה that follows: one who fasts on ערב שבת completes the fast.

phrases.english: Rather: this question was before he heard the ruling,
phrases.notes: רבה's question to רב הונא came before רב הונא heard רב's ruling.

phrases.english: and this statement was after he heard it,
phrases.notes: The ruling quoted by מר זוטרא came later.

phrases.english: here too: this question was before he heard the ruling,
phrases.notes: Now the same answer is applied to רב יהודה.

phrases.english: and this statement was after he heard it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 2 and uses the same answer to cancel the proof in Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Chronological distinction: the earlier question came before the teacher heard the ruling, and the later statement came after.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because רבה got no answer from רב יהודה, we might think רב יהודה never had a ruling on ערב שבת, so his statement must be limited to other cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The silence happened before he heard רב's ruling, so it says nothing about his later position. His ruling can include ערב שבת.

steps.title: The final ruling: one fasts and completes the fast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates מר זוטרא's teaching in the name of רב הונא as the final ruling. The הלכה is that people fast and complete the fast, even on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא taught in the name of רב הונא: The הלכה is that people fast and complete the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes, as its own clear conclusion, the ruling it mentioned in passing earlier. This settles the practical question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 2 this ruling was only quoted to build an argument. Here the גמרא states it on its own as the final הלכה. Note the plural form (מתענין ומשלימין), which states the rule for the public in general.

keyTerms.meaning: People fast and complete the fast (plural form)
The practical law

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: one who fasts on ערב שבת completes the fast until nightfall, as מר זוטרא taught in the name of רב הונא.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a pointless repetition of Step 2. There the ruling was quoted only as a tool in the argument. Here the גמרא states it directly as the final ruling.

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra taught in the name of Rav Huna:
The halacha is that people fast and complete the fast.
phrases.notes: This applies even on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the contradiction is resolved, the גמרא restates on its own the ruling it quoted earlier in Step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is that one fasts and completes the fast on ערב שבת, as taught by מר זוטרא in the name of רב הונא.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter בכל מערבין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the third chapter of עירובין, פרק בכל מערבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'בכל מערבין'.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter ends here. This line is a farewell formula that says, "We will come back to you, בכל מערבין."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion about fasting on ערב שבת was the last topic of this chapter. With this line, that whole unit is closed. Nothing new is argued here. It is a closing marker, and a brand-new topic starts right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you." This is the formula said when finishing a chapter.
"With everything one may make an עירוב." This is the name of the chapter being closed.

steps.whatToRemember: The last ruling of the chapter stands: people fast and complete the fast, even on ערב שבת.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'With everything one may make an eruv'
phrases.notes: This is the usual line said when finishing a chapter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter whose last topic, fasting on ערב שבת, was concluded in Step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Chapter three of עירובין, בכל מערבין, is complete.

steps.title: A person taken out of his שבת limit by force has only four אמות
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that someone carried beyond his תחום שבת against his will, by נכרים or by a רוח רעה, may move only four אמות where he ends up.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person whom non-Jews took out of his limit, or whom an evil spirit (temporary insanity) took out, has only four אמות in which to move.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a new משנה. The first case is a person who was forced out of his Shabbat limit. He may now move only four אמות from where he stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person may walk 2000 אמות around the place where he settled for שבת. This person was taken out without his own choice, and he has no valid place of residence where he now is. So he is limited to the smallest space, four אמות. The point is that being forced out does not give him a new full תחום.

keyTerms.meaning: "Our משנה." This marks the start of the משנה text.
Non-Jews, here meaning people who took him by force.
An "evil spirit," meaning a temporary loss of sanity.
Four cubits. This is the basic personal space every person has on שבת.

steps.confusionAlert: Four אמות is not his whole Shabbat limit returning to him. It is the small space every person always has wherever he is. He lost the usual 2000 אמות because he left his תחום against his will.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One whom they took out
phrases.notes: These are also the opening words that name the new chapter, מי שהוציאוהו.

phrases.english: gentiles, or an evil spirit
phrases.notes: Two kinds of forced removal: by other people, or by his own temporary insanity.

phrases.english: he has only four cubits.
phrases.notes: These four אמות are measured from where he is now standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter and topic right after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person forcibly removed beyond his תחום שבת is limited to four אמות where he ends up.

steps.title: If he is brought back, it is as if he never left
steps.stepSummary: If the person who was taken out is returned to his original תחום, he gets his full original limit back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they brought him back, it is as though he never went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second case. If the same person is brought back into his original Shabbat limit, his original rights come back completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving against his will did not cancel his original place of residence for Shabbat. Once he is back inside it, he may walk the full original תחום again, as if nothing happened. This tells us the four-אמות limit only applies while he is stuck outside.

keyTerms.meaning: "They returned him."
"As though he never went out."

phrases.english: If they returned him
phrases.notes: This could be the נכרים bringing him back, or the רוח רעה bringing him back.

phrases.english: it is as though he had never left.
phrases.notes: His original 2000-אמה limit is fully restored.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same case and shows what happens when the forced removal is reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forcibly removed person who is returned keeps his original תחום, as if he never left.

steps.title: A dispute about a person placed inside a walled city or an animal pen
steps.stepSummary: If the person was brought into another enclosed area, the תנאים disagree. One pair says he may walk the whole area, and the other pair says he has only four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they brought him to another (walled) city, or put him in an animal pen or stable: רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה say he may walk through all of it. רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא say he has only four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה presents a third case with a מחלוקת. The question is what happens if the person was placed inside an enclosed space, such as a walled city or an animal pen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה hold that the whole enclosed area counts like his four אמות, so he may walk all of it. רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא hold that walls do not help a person who was brought there against his will, so he is still limited to four אמות. The disagreement is only about enclosed spaces. In open land, everyone agrees he has four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: A different city, understood to be surrounded by walls.
A pen, meaning an enclosure for sheep.
A stable, meaning an enclosure for animals.
"He walks all of it," meaning the entire enclosed area.

steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת is the base of the chapter. The גמרא will go on to explore whether walls make an enclosed area count as four אמות.

phrases.english: If they brought him to a different city
phrases.notes: The city is understood to be surrounded by walls.

phrases.english: or put him into a pen or a stable
phrases.notes: Both are enclosures for animals.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya say:
phrases.notes: This is the lenient opinion.

phrases.english: He may walk about the entire area.
phrases.notes: The whole enclosed area is treated like his four אמות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva say:
phrases.notes: This is the strict opinion.

phrases.english: He has only four cubits.
phrases.notes: The walls do not expand his area.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹלִיכוּהוּ לְעִיר אַחֶרֶת נְתָנוּהוּ בְּדִיר אוֹ בְּסַהַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third case to the same scenario: the person is moved into an enclosed space, and the תנאים disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rule that he may walk the entire enclosed area. רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא rule that he is limited to four אמות.

steps.title: The ship story: who walked the whole ship and who stayed in four אמות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells a story that shows the dispute from the previous step in real life. On a ship taken out to sea, two sages walked the whole ship and two sages stayed within four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident when they came from Plandarsin and their ship sailed out to sea. רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה walked through the whole ship. רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא did not move beyond four אמות, because they wanted to be strict on themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a true story that illustrates the argument from step 8: a person brought into another enclosed area, here a ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ship is like an enclosed area, so רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה treated it as one big space they could walk freely. רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא limited themselves to four אמות. The phrase 'they wanted to be strict on themselves' hints that their behavior may have been a personal חומרא rather than the strict law, and the גמרא will look into this later.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or true story, brought as a practical example
Sailed out (far into the sea)
Ship
To be strict on themselves (a personal stringency)

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'they wanted to be strict on themselves' can be misleading. They suggest that רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא were not necessarily saying the law requires four אמות. They may simply have been stricter for themselves.

phrases.english: There was an incident when they came from Plandarsin,
phrases.notes: Plandarsin was a port city (Brundisium).

phrases.english: and their ship sailed out far into the sea (on Shabbat).
phrases.notes: They were carried out of their limit without choosing it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
walked through all of it (the whole ship),
phrases.notes: They treated the ship as one enclosed area.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva
did not move beyond four cubits,
because they wanted to be strict on themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life story that shows the dispute from step 8 in action.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the ship, רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה walked everywhere, while רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא stayed within four אמות as a personal stringency.

steps.title: Arriving at port after dark: may we get off?
steps.stepSummary: Another time, the ship reached port only after nightfall. The others asked רבן גמליאל whether they were allowed to get off the ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: One time they did not enter the port until it had already gotten dark. They said to רבן גמליאל: what about us getting off the ship?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a second ship story and asks a practical question. This sets up רבן גמליאל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that שבת began while they were still at sea, outside the city's תחום. If so, they would be limited to four אמות and could not walk into the city. They are asking whether they had already 'arrived' inside the limit before שבת started.

keyTerms.meaning: Port or harbor
It got dark (nightfall, the start of שבת)
To get off (the ship)

phrases.english: One time they did not enter the port
until it had gotten dark,
phrases.notes: That is, after שבת had begun.

phrases.english: they said to Rabban Gamliel:
What about us getting off (the ship)?
phrases.notes: Meaning: is it permitted for us to get off and walk into the city?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: מָה אָנוּ לֵירֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ship story. This one is about arriving at port after שבת has begun.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether they may get off the ship and walk in the city, even though they reached port after dark.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: we were inside the limit before dark
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל permits them to get off, because he had seen that the ship was already inside the city's תחום before nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: you are permitted to get off, because I was already watching, and we were inside the city's limit before it got dark.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל answers the question from step 10 and says they may get off the ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is where the person is at the moment שבת begins. Since the ship was already inside the city's תחום before dark, their שביתה, their 'home base' for שבת, was acquired in the city. So they may walk through the city and its limit even though they actually docked after dark.

keyTerms.meaning: You are permitted
Watching or observing
The place a person 'settles' for שבת when it begins, which sets his limit

steps.whatToRemember: Your שבת limit is set by where you are when שבת begins. רבן גמליאל saw that they were already within the city's תחום before dark, so they could get off.

phrases.english: He said to them: You are permitted (to get off),
for I was already watching,
and we were inside the (city's) limit
before it got dark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They may get off, because the ship entered the city's תחום before nightfall, so they acquired their שבת place inside the city's limit.

steps.title: Three things that push a person against his will
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא saying that three things make a person act against his own will and the will of his Maker: נכרים, רוח רעה, and harsh poverty.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: three things make a person go against his own will and the will of his Creator. They are: non-Jews, an evil spirit, and the harsh pressures of poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא. It is connected to the משנה because the משנה mentioned נכרים and a רוח רעה taking a person out of his limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה spoke of a person taken out of his תחום by נכרים or a רוח רעה, which is against his will. This ברייתא lists those same forces, plus extreme poverty, as things that can make a person break both his own wishes and ה׳'s will. The ברייתא adds poverty to the two forces already named in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Against the will of his Maker (ה׳)
The harsh, crushing pressures of poverty

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the technical law of the משנה to a bigger human idea: some forces push people to act against their own will, and a person in that situation deserves understanding.

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא discussion on this משנה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught (in a baraita):
Three things cause a person to go against
his own will and the will of his Maker,
and these are: non-Jews,
and an evil spirit, and the harsh pressures of poverty.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מַעֲבִירִין אֶת הָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא with a ברייתא connected to the forces mentioned in the משנה (step 6).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three things push a person against his own will and ה׳'s will: נכרים, רוח רעה, and harsh poverty.

steps.title: Why does this list matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference comes from knowing the three things listed in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need to know the list from the previous step: נכרים, רוח רעה, and harsh poverty. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא described a fact about people: these three things make a person act against his will. The גמרא wants to know what we are supposed to do with this information.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make? What practical result comes from this?

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא about three things that push a person against his own will and his Maker's will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the practical purpose of the ברייתא in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical lesson comes from knowing that נכרים, רוח רעה, and harsh poverty push a person against his will.

steps.title: So that we pray for mercy about them
steps.stepSummary: Knowing these three dangers teaches us to pray to be saved from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: To ask for mercy about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the list is there so people will pray to be spared from these three hardships.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is not just a description. Because these things can push even a good person into sin, a person should ask ה׳ to protect him from them.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask for mercy, to pray
About them, concerning them

phrases.english: To request mercy concerning them.
phrases.notes: That is, to pray to be protected from these three things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical purpose is to pray to be saved from these hardships.

steps.title: Three people who never see גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: A related ברייתא lists three sufferers who are spared from גיהנם, and a יש אומרים adds a fourth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three people do not see the face of גיהנם: those in extreme poverty, those with stomach illness, and those oppressed by the authorities. Some say: also a man who has a bad wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא on a similar theme of heavy suffering. It lists people whose pain in this world spares them from גיהנם, and a second opinion adds one more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that their suffering in this world already makes up for their sins. The first opinion names three kinds of people. The יש אומרים adds a man stuck with a bad wife, and that creates a disagreement the גמרא will now explain.

keyTerms.meaning: גיהנם, the place where souls are punished after death
The harshest, most crushing poverty
People with stomach or intestinal illness
The authorities: oppressive rulers, or according to some, creditors
A bad, harsh wife

phrases.english: Three do not see the face of Gehenna,
phrases.notes: Their suffering in this world atones for them.

phrases.english: and they are: those in the depths of poverty,
and those with intestinal illness, and the authorities (those oppressed by them).
phrases.notes: Some explain this as people oppressed by creditors.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אִשָּׁה רָעָה.
phrases.english: And some say: even one who has a bad wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel 'three things' ברייתא about heavy suffering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Extreme poverty, intestinal illness, and oppression by the authorities spare a person from גיהנם. The יש אומרים adds a bad wife.

steps.title: Why does the first opinion leave out a bad wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first opinion does not include a man with a bad wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the first opinion did not count a bad wife as a suffering that spares a person from גיהנם. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living with a bad wife sounds like real suffering. So it seems strange that the first opinion leaves it out.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? What does the other opinion hold?

steps.confusionAlert: ואידך appears twice in this section and points at a different side each time. Here it means the first opinion, which does NOT include a bad wife.

phrases.english: And the other (opinion)?
phrases.notes: Why does the first opinion not list a bad wife?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the first opinion in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first opinion does not count a bad wife.

steps.title: He can divorce her
steps.stepSummary: A bad wife is not counted because there is a מצוה to divorce her, so he can end the suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a מצוה to divorce a bad wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first opinion leaves out a bad wife because a man is told to divorce her, so he does not have to stay in that suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three people on the list are stuck in their suffering and cannot escape it. A man with a bad wife can escape it through divorce. Since his suffering is in his own hands to fix, it does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to divorce her

phrases.english: A bad wife, it is a מצוה to divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Divorce is available and is even a מצוה, so this suffering can be ended.

steps.title: Why does the second opinion include a bad wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks how the יש אומרים can include a bad wife if divorce is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to the יש אומרים and asks why they include a bad wife, since he could just divorce her. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer seemed to show that this suffering can be escaped. So the יש אומרים must hold that divorce is not always a real way out.

phrases.english: And the other (opinion)?
phrases.notes: This time it asks about the יש אומרים, who do include a bad wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the other side of the disagreement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the יש אומרים include a bad wife despite the option of divorce.

steps.title: Sometimes he cannot divorce her
steps.stepSummary: Sometimes divorce is not practical: her כתובה may be too large, or they may have children together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes her כתובה is large. Or he has children from her, and he cannot divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the יש אומרים include a bad wife because in real life a man is sometimes trapped. He may not afford her כתובה, or he may not be able to send away the mother of his children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that divorce is a מצוה. The question is whether it is always possible. When money or children block a divorce, the man is just as stuck as the other sufferers, so his pain also atones for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
Her כתובה payment is large
Alternatively, or else
He cannot divorce

steps.whatToRemember: Three sufferers do not see גיהנם: the very poor, the sick in the stomach, and the oppressed. The יש אומרים add a man with a bad wife, because sometimes a large כתובה or shared children keep him from divorcing her.

phrases.english: Sometimes her ketubba is large.
phrases.notes: He cannot afford to pay it, so he cannot divorce her.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי, אִית לֵיהּ בָּנִים מִינַּהּ,
phrases.english: Alternatively, he has children from her,
and he is not able to divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by showing that divorce is not always realistic.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A large כתובה or shared children can make divorce impossible, leaving him trapped in suffering.

steps.title: What practical difference does the list of sufferers make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical lesson comes from knowing which sufferers are spared from גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference of this teaching?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it matters to know that certain sufferers are spared from גיהנם. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing who is spared from גיהנם seems to have no practical effect in this world. The גמרא wants to know what a person should actually do with this information.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
גיהנם, the place of punishment after death

phrases.english: For what does it make a practical difference?
phrases.notes: This refers back to the ברייתא of sufferers spared from גיהנם (steps 15-19).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having finished explaining the list, the גמרא now asks what its practical use is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical lesson comes from knowing that these sufferers are spared from גיהנם?

steps.title: To accept suffering with love
steps.stepSummary: The practical lesson is that such a sufferer should accept his pain with love.
steps.simpleTranslation: To accept them with love.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this teaching tells a sufferer to accept his suffering lovingly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person knows his suffering spares him from גיהנם, he can see it as something good rather than complain about it. So the teaching shapes his attitude in this world.

keyTerms.meaning: To accept
With love

steps.whatToRemember: The list of sufferers spared from גיהנם teaches a sufferer to accept his pain with love.

phrases.english: To accept them with love.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The teaching tells the sufferer to accept his suffering lovingly, since it saves him from גיהנם.

steps.title: Three illnesses that can kill suddenly while talking
steps.stepSummary: A related teaching lists three kinds of patients who may die suddenly even while they seem well enough to talk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three kinds of people die while they are still talking: those with intestinal illness, a woman giving birth, and one with dropsy (edema).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another list on a similar theme of illness. This one names three conditions in which a person can die suddenly while still talking normally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first list was about sufferers who are spared from גיהנם. This new list is about people whose death can come without warning. They seem healthy enough to hold a conversation, yet they may die at any moment.

keyTerms.meaning: They die while still talking, meaning a sudden death
Intestinal illness
A woman giving birth
Dropsy or edema, a swelling illness

steps.confusionAlert: Here חַיָּה does not mean an animal. It means a woman in childbirth.

phrases.english: Three kinds of people die while they are still conversing,
and these are they: one with intestinal illness,
and a woman in childbirth, and one with edema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel list of three on the theme of illness, following the list of sufferers in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People with intestinal illness, women in childbirth, and those with edema can die suddenly while they still seem well.

steps.title: What practical difference does this list make?
steps.stepSummary: Again the גמרא asks what practical lesson this list teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question it asked before: why do we need to know this? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא uses the same question here as in step 20. Each list is expected to teach something a person can actually act on.

keyTerms.meaning: Three, the number of items in the list being discussed

phrases.english: For what does it make a practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical use of the list in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What should be done differently because these patients might die suddenly?

steps.title: Prepare burial shrouds in advance
steps.stepSummary: The practical lesson is to prepare burial shrouds for such patients ahead of time.
steps.simpleTranslation: To prepare shrouds for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we should prepare burial shrouds for these patients early, because their death could come suddenly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These patients look well, so people might not think to get ready. The list warns us that death can come without warning, so the preparations should be made in advance.

keyTerms.meaning: To prepare or get ready
Provisions; here, burial shrouds (תכריכין)

steps.whatToRemember: For patients who may die suddenly, shrouds are prepared ahead of time.

phrases.english: To prepare shrouds for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 and closes the side discussion about sufferers.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Prepare shrouds in advance, since death may come suddenly.

steps.title: One who knowingly left the תחום has only four אמות
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה, רב נחמן quotes שמואל: a person who knowingly went beyond the תחום has only four אמות to walk in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: If someone went out knowingly, he has only four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about someone taken beyond the תחום שבת. It quotes רב נחמן's ruling for a person who went out on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that someone taken out by נכרים has only four אמות. רב נחמן applies the same limit to someone who left knowingly. This ruling will be challenged right away.

keyTerms.meaning: He went out knowingly, on purpose
Four cubits, the small area a person may move within
The שבת boundary a person may not walk past

steps.whyThisMatters: This brings the גמרא back to the main halachic topic of the פרק: what happens to someone who ends up outside the תחום.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
If one went out knowingly,
he has only four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion and returns to the משנה of מי שהוציאוהו נכרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who knowingly left the תחום may move only four אמות.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if even someone taken out by force has only four אמות, then of course someone who left on purpose does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! Now, if someone whom נכרים took out has only four אמות, do we need to be told about someone who went out knowingly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's ruling as too obvious to need saying. It uses a קל וחומר from the משנה's case of being taken out by force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person forced out did nothing wrong, and he still gets only four אמות. The person who left on purpose deserves no better, so the law for him seems automatic. The ruling therefore looks like it teaches nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new
Now, if even...; it opens a קל וחומר
One whom non-Jews took out (the משנה's case)
Is it even necessary to say?

phrases.english: This is obvious!
Now, if one whom gentiles took out
has only four cubits,
is it necessary to say so about one who went out knowingly?!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא הַשְׁתָּא מִי שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּהוּ נׇכְרִים אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's ruling in step 25 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's statement that one who knowingly left has only four אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if a person forced out, who is blameless, gets only four אמות, then one who left on purpose surely gets no more. So the statement adds nothing.

steps.title: Rewording: he meant someone who came back on purpose
steps.stepSummary: To avoid the problem that the rule is too obvious, the גמרא rewords רב נחמן's statement. It now says that someone who returned on purpose has only four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: if he came back on purpose, he has only four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the obviousness problem by changing what רב נחמן said. The case is now someone taken out by force who then walked back in on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here נכרים took him out against his will, and then he came back into the תחום knowingly. The new point would be that coming back on his own does not fix anything. He still has only four אמות. This is no longer an obvious קל וחומר from the משנה's case.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the גמרא rewords a statement to fix a problem
He returned knowingly, on purpose
Four cubits, the small area a person stranded outside his תחום may move in

phrases.english: Rather, say: if he returned knowingly —
phrases.notes: Meaning he was taken out by gentiles and then came back by himself.

phrases.english: he has only four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the obviousness challenge of step 26 by rewording רב נחמן's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case of the מימרא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן was talking about someone who went out on purpose, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was talking about someone forced out who returned on purpose. That person still has only four אמות.

steps.title: Objection: the משנה already implies this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the rewording is also unnecessary. The משנה says that if נכרים brought him back, it is as if he never left. This implies that if he came back on his own, he has only four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too we already learned: if gentiles brought him back, it is as if he never left. Only when they brought him back is it as if he never left. But if gentiles took him out and he came back on his own, he has only four אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new version. It shows that the משנה's wording already teaches this rule by implication.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה specifically says "נכרים brought him back." That suggests the good outcome depends on them bringing him back. So if he came back on his own, he does not get that outcome and stays with four אמות. So רב נחמן would again be adding nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: This too we already learned (in the משנה)
Gentiles brought him back
As if he never left
An inference drawn from the exact wording of a text

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say this rule outright. The גמרא is reading it into the משנה's wording: "only if they returned him" implies "but not if he returned himself."

phrases.english: This too we have learned:
If gentiles returned him, it is as though he never left.
phrases.notes: These words are quoted from the משנה.

phrases.english: It is specifically when they returned him that it is as though he never left,
but if gentiles took him out and he returned knowingly —
he has only four cubits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rewording in step 27 as redundant with the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version of רב נחמן about someone who returned knowingly
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording "if gentiles returned him" already implies that returning on one's own gives only four אמות. So the statement is redundant.

steps.title: Second rewording: left on purpose, brought back by force
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again. רב נחמן meant someone who went out on purpose and was then brought back by נכרים. That person still has only four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: if he went out on purpose and gentiles brought him back, he has only four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new version of רב נחמן's statement to escape the last challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the leaving was on purpose and the return was forced. The new point would be that being forcibly returned does not undo his deliberate exit. He is still limited to four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: He went out knowingly, on purpose
The שבת boundary beyond which one may not walk

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵימָא, יָצָא לְדַעַת וְהֶחְזִירוּהוּ נׇכְרִים —
phrases.english: Rather, say: if he went out knowingly and gentiles returned him —
he has only four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא, יָצָא לְדַעַת וְהֶחְזִירוּהוּ נׇכְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28's challenge with a different reading of רב נחמן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case of the מימרא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן was talking about someone who returned on his own, which the משנה already implies.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was talking about someone who left on purpose and was returned by force. That person still has only four אמות.

steps.title: Objection: this too is implied by the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again. The משנה says that if they took him out and brought him back, it is as if he never left. That implies the leniency applies only when both the exit and the return were forced, not when he left on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too we already learned: if they took him out and brought him back, it is as if he never left. Only when they both took him out and brought him back is it as if he never left. But if he went out on purpose, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second rewording as well. Once again it shows the rule can be read out of the משנה's wording. The answer will come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes a case where נכרים did both the taking out and the bringing back. The implication is that "as if he never left" requires both to be forced. So if he left on purpose, being brought back does not help, and רב נחמן seems to add nothing new again.

keyTerms.meaning: They took him out and brought him back
No (Aramaic): that rule does not apply

steps.whyThisMatters: This pressure sets up the גמרא's final answer: the משנה might have been read as teaching two separate cases, so רב נחמן's statement is still needed.

phrases.english: This too we have learned:
If they took him out and returned him, it is as though he never left.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹצִיאוּהוּ וְהֶחְזִירוּהוּ — הוּא דִּכְאִילּוּ לֹא יָצָא,
phrases.english: It is specifically when they took him out and returned him that it is as though he never left,
but if he went out knowingly — no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second rewording in step 29 as redundant with the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version of רב נחמן about someone who left knowingly and was returned by נכרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's case of being taken out and returned by force implies that leaving on purpose gets no leniency. So the statement is redundant.

steps.title: רב נחמן's rule blocks a split reading of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 30. Without רב נחמן's rule, we might have read the משנה 'לצדדין', as two separate cases. In that reading, someone who left on purpose and was brought back by נכרים would be treated as if he never left. רב נחמן teaches that this is wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought the משנה teaches two separate cases. In the first, נכרים took him out and he came back on purpose, so he has only four אמות. In the second, he left on purpose and נכרים brought him back, so it is as if he never left. רב נחמן's statement teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן's statement by showing it is not obvious after all. It prevents a possible misreading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 said the משנה already implies that only a fully forced trip, out and back, counts as 'never left.' The גמרא answers that the משנה's wording could also be split into two separate cases. On that split reading, being forcibly returned would be enough to erase a willful exit. רב נחמן rules this out: if the exit was on purpose, a forced return does not help, and he has only four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said / thought (introduces a mistaken assumption)
It teaches separate cases (each part of the sentence is its own case)
On purpose, knowingly
He teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: Final position on רב נחמן's case: someone who left the תחום on purpose and was brought back by נכרים has only four אמות. A forced return cannot fix a willful exit.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'לצדדין' reading is the mistaken idea, not the conclusion. רב נחמן's rule exists precisely to reject it.

phrases.english: You might have said
phrases.notes: Introduces the mistake that רב נחמן comes to block.

phrases.english: it teaches separate cases:
one whom non-Jews took out
and he returned on purpose
has only four cubits,
but if he went out on purpose
and non-Jews brought him back
it is as if he never left,
so he teaches us (that this is not so).
phrases.notes: רב נחמן's rule shows we shouldn't split the case up that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 30 by showing the משנה could have been misread.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement is needed to block a possible misreading of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is 'לצדדין': a willful exit followed by a forced return counts as never having left.
steps.terutzMaskana: A willful exit followed by a forced return still leaves him with only four אמות.

steps.title: What if a person limited to four cubits must relieve himself?
steps.stepSummary: רבה is asked a practical question. A person is stuck with only four אמות and needs to relieve himself. What is he allowed to do?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked Rabbah: if he needed to relieve himself, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. Students ask רבה how a person limited to four אמות can relieve himself with dignity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone limited to four אמות cannot move away to find a private place. The question is whether the four-אמות restriction gives way so he can avoid public embarrassment.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him (a question put to a teacher)
He needed to relieve himself
What is the law?

phrases.english: They asked Rabbah:
If he needed to relieve himself, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Refers to the person restricted to four אמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the case of a person who has only four אמות and asks about a practical need.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person limited to four אמות may go beyond them to relieve himself privately.

steps.title: Human dignity overrides the restriction
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers with the principle of כבוד הבריות. Human dignity is so important that it pushes aside a לא תעשה. So the person may go beyond his four אמות to relieve himself privately.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: great is human dignity, which pushes aside a negative commandment of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. Because of human dignity, the person may leave his four אמות to find a private place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה applies the general principle of כבוד הבריות to this case. The four-אמות and תחום limits involved here are rabbinic. Protecting a person from humiliation is weighty enough to set them aside.

keyTerms.meaning: Human dignity
Pushes aside, overrides
A negative commandment (prohibition)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לא תעשה שבתורה' does not mean a person may break any תורה prohibition for dignity. The גמרא in ברכות (19b) explains that it refers to 'לא תסור', the תורה's command to obey the חכמים. So the principle overrides rabbinic rules, such as the rabbinic תחום limits here.
steps.whyThisMatters: כבוד הבריות is a major halachic principle that appears across ש״ס. Here it gives a practical leniency.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Great is human dignity,
which overrides a negative commandment of the Torah.
phrases.notes: The commandment meant here is 'לא תסור', so this can override rabbinic rules.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He may go beyond his four אמות to relieve himself, because כבוד הבריות overrides rabbinic restrictions.

steps.title: A clever person walks back into his original limit
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of נהרדעא add practical advice. Since he is already allowed to walk, a smart person should head back into his original תחום. Once he is inside with permission, he stays inside and regains the whole area.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars of נהרדעא said: if he is clever, he will walk into his original תחום. Since he entered, he has entered.
steps.whatsHappening: נהרדעי build on רבה's leniency with a practical tip. A clever person uses his permitted walk to return inside his original תחום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה allowed him to leave the four אמות to relieve himself. נהרדעי point out that if he walks toward his original תחום and enters it, he entered with permission. Once inside, he is like everyone else there and has the full area again.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of נהרדעא
Clever, smart
Once he has entered, he has entered (and may stay)

phrases.english: The scholars of Neharde'a said:
If he is clever,
he will enter into his original limit,
and once he has entered, he has entered.
phrases.notes: He entered with permission, so he may remain inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical extension to רבה's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person allowed to move for כבוד הבריות may walk back into his original תחום, and once inside he regains the full area.

steps.title: Produce taken out and brought back keeps its place
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules about objects rather than people. Produce taken outside the תחום and brought back keeps its original place, even if this was done on purpose. It may be carried throughout the whole תחום. The reason is that produce never moves by choice, so it always counts as forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: produce that went out beyond the תחום and came back, even if this was done on purpose, has not lost its place. What is the reason? They are forced.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling, now about produce. רב פפא says produce returned to its תחום keeps its place even when it was moved deliberately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a person, we saw that a willful exit can cost him his place. Produce has no will of its own, so whoever carried it, even on purpose, it counts as אנוס (forced). That is why it does not lose its place.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce, fruit
Deliberately, on purpose
They did not lose their place (keep their original תחום)
Forced, acting without choice

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling sets up the next step, where רב יוסף בר שמעיה challenges רב פפא from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
produce that went out beyond the limit and came back,
even if it was done on purpose,
has not lost its place.
What is the reason?
They are forced.
phrases.notes: The produce itself had no choice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: פֵּירוֹת שֶׁיָּצְאוּ חוּץ לַתְּחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from people to objects, applying the idea of forced movement to produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce taken out of the תחום and returned, even deliberately, keeps its place, because produce is always considered forced.

steps.title: A challenge to רב פפא from רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר שמעיה cites רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. They say produce stays forbidden until it is brought back by mistake. This implies that a return done on purpose does not help, which contradicts רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר שמעיה challenged רב פפא: רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב say the produce is always forbidden until it is returned to its place by mistake. So by mistake, yes; on purpose, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's rule from Step 35 using a statement of תנאים. Those תנאים say only an accidental return makes the produce permitted again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said that produce always counts as forced, so even a deliberate return restores its original place. The תנאים here say the return must be שוגג. That wording implies a deliberate (מזיד) return does not help, so the person's intent does matter for produce.

keyTerms.meaning: They are always forbidden
By mistake, unintentionally
On purpose, deliberately
Yes

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר שְׁמַעְיָה לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Shemaya challenged Rav Pappa:
phrases.notes: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ means he's challenging him from a teaching of the תנאים.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov say:
They are always forbidden,
phrases.notes: Referring to the produce that left the תחום.

phrases.english: until they are returned to their place by mistake.
By mistake, yes; on purpose, no!
phrases.notes: Reading between the lines, this goes against what רב פפא said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר שְׁמַעְיָה לְרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's ruling in Step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that produce returned on purpose keeps its original place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תנאים require the return to be שוגג. That implies a מזיד return does not help, so intent does matter for produce.

steps.title: This is a dispute among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the matter is a dispute between תנאים. רב פפא can rely on another tannaitic source; the rest of the ברייתא, on the next amud, shows which one. It begins citing a ברייתא: produce taken out by mistake may be eaten, but produce taken out on purpose may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute among תנאים. As it was taught in a ברייתא: produce that was taken outside the תחום by mistake may be eaten. If it was taken out on purpose, it may not be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא. It says the challenge only reflects one opinion among the תנאים, and other תנאים disagree. It begins quoting a ברייתא that shows the different views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא answers that the challenging source is not the only tannaitic view, and it shows that the question of שוגג and מזיד with produce is debated among תנאים. The lines quoted here give only the opening clause of the ברייתא. The rest of the ברייתא, with the opinion רב פפא can rely on, continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among the תנאים
Produce, fruit
They may be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume from these lines alone where רבי נחמיה stands. The continuation of the ברייתא on the next amud shows which tannaitic view supports רב פפא.

phrases.english: It is a dispute among tanna'im,
as it was taught: produce that went out beyond the Shabbat limit,
if by mistake, it may be eaten;
if on purpose, it may not be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tannaitic dispute: רב פפא follows a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought רב פפא contradicts an accepted tannaitic ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The issue is debated among תנאים, so רב פפא is following one side of that debate.
